newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns Vatican not to meddle in its affairs.
newsitem.headline: China warns Vatican not to meddle in its affairs.

text.p: Beijing responded on Thursday to an appeal from Pope John Paul to legalise the Roman Catholic Church, saying it wanted better relations with the Vatican but would brook no interference in China's internal affairs.
"The Vatican must... stop interfering in China's internal affairs, including using religion to interfere in China's affairs," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said by telephone.
Pope John Paul this week appealed to China's communist rulers to legalise the Roman Catholic Church and allow its Chinese members to worship openly.
China allows Catholics to worship openly only if they belong to the Catholic Patriotic Association, which is backed by the Chinese Communist Party and does not recognise the Pope's authority.
A bishop with the association rebuked the Vatican for its stance towards religious activity in China, saying believers of many faiths led happy and normal religious lives in China.
"He (the Pope) doesn't understand China's actual conditions," Bishop Zong Huaide said by telephone.
The Foreign Ministry spokesman said China hoped to improve relations with the Vatican, but added that the Vatican would first have to sever relations with Beijing's rival Taiwan.
"The Vatican must break off its so-called 'diplomatic relations' with Taiwan and recognise the People's Republic of China as the sole legal government of China," the spokesman said.

Official links between Beijing and the Vatican were cut in the 1950s with the Vatican's recognition of Taiwan, which Beijing has regarded as a rebel province since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
The Beijing-backed Catholic church claims some four million members while another several million people are believed to worship underground.
Western human rights groups have said Beijing has stepped up harassment of unauthorised Catholic and Protestant groups in recent years.
